purpose: Individual reconciliation against each existing scope. Completed review is not product certification or proof that every gap is resolved.

applications.name: Logseq
E3: Exporter UUID/timestamp/ontology options and SQLite backup failure cleanup are concretely described in source. No populated graph including assets, properties, references and file-to-DB conversion has been independently reconstructed. A successful database-copy mechanism alone does not establish complete graph semantics or safe existing-destination recovery.
E5: Backup failure cleanup can remove its destination, while the collected evidence does not establish effective caller destination safety, plugin authority, synchronization-conflict control or inspectable correction for DB graph mutations. Export options and source error handling are not whole-workflow oversight.
longevity: E3 is not established for Logseq's existing essential-record scope. The previous Longevity finding is replaced by Not assessed, not a verified failure or a positive placeholder.
transparency: The positive control observations above do not yet establish whole-scope E5. The methodology requires that minimum before a positive Transparency and Control finding; the previous positive finding is therefore withdrawn to Not assessed, not changed to Does not meet.
applications.remaining: A populated DB independently queried, complete asset-inclusive graph export/restore, file-to-DB conversion, task/property/ref fidelity, automatic-backup retention and cross-version outcomes. E5 needs caller destination safety, plugin and DB-sync authority, change inspection and recovery/retention boundaries.
applications.current_remaining: A populated DB independently queried, complete asset-inclusive graph export/restore, file-to-DB conversion, task/property/ref fidelity, automatic-backup retention and cross-version outcomes. E5 needs caller destination safety, plugin and DB-sync authority, change inspection and recovery/retention boundaries.

The prior positive finding is withdrawn; recorded storage and portability strengths remain facts, not a verified failure.

Effective duplicate handling, import/checkpoint configuration, source mutation visibility and recourse after bad imports are not sufficiently covered for whole-scope E5.
